entries.title: Psalms 74:1
segments:
Title, of Asaph; as this psalm must be referred to the destruction of the temple by the Chaldeans, many understand "Asaph" as standing for Asaph's family; as several psalms are, according to one interpretation, ascribed to "the sons of Korah," that is, to some one of his descendants. 
 
  The sheep of thy pasture; Israel, as the peculiar people of God, and especially the pious among this people. 
 
The fatherly corrections which God inflicts on his people, and which are indications of his love, may sometimes be mistaken by them for expressions of anger; but in the end they will see that it was in kindness to their souls.

entries.title: Psalms 74:2
segments: The rod of thine inheritance; or, the tribe of thine inheritance, the word tribe being used collectively for the whole people.

entries.title: Psalms 74:3
segments: Lift up thy feet; that is, march forth from thy hiding-place and look upon the desolations caused by the enemy.

entries.title: Psalms 74:4
segments: Thy congregations; rather, thy places of assembly.  The Hebrew word is the same that is rendered "synagogues," in

, where see note. 
 
  There ensigns for signs; they have set up their own heathenish ensigns, as tokens of their dominion, where once the symbol of God's presence and power stood. 
 
  Ensigns; tokens of authority.

entries.title: Psalms 74:5
segments: A man was famous--thick trees; the meaning of this and the following verse, according to our version, seems to be, that once men showed their power and skill in cutting down forest-trees for useful purposes, such as building; but now they make themselves famous as destroyers.  We may, however, render literally thus: "He [the enemy] makes himself known as one who lifts up axes upon thick trees.  And now they break down," etc.  That is, he proceeds with the cedar-work of the temple as one does with the common trees of the forest, destroying without thought or care.

entries.title: Psalms 74:6
segments: Carved work; with which the place of worship was adorned.

entries.title: Psalms 74:8
segments: All the synagogue of--the land; or, all the places of assembly in the land.  See notes to

.  There is no necessity of understanding this of the Jewish synagogues, which were first built at a later date.  None of the ancient versions so translate it. 
 
Men may be so blinded and hardened by sin as to attempt the utter destruction of the Lord's people; but in due time he will arise, plead his own cause, and bring destruction upon those who continue to oppose it.

entries.title: Psalms 74:9
segments:
Our signs; tokens of God's presence, especially as manifested in the gift of prophecy. 
 
  How long; how long our troubles will continue.

entries.title: Psalms 74:11
segments: Withdrawest thou thy hand; delaying to deliver them.

entries.title: Psalms 74:12
segments: Working salvation; in the deliverance of Israel from Egypt and from all their enemies.

entries.title: Psalms 74:13
segments:
Dragons; monsters of the deep; representing the great and powerful opposers of divine truth.  So also leviathan in the following verse. 
 
Past deliverances of God's people encourage them to expect his interposition in future, and to look to him for the aid which they need.

entries.title: Psalms 74:16
segments: The vicissitudes of the seasons are all ordered by God, and he who can make day and night, summer and winter, can do all things which the good of his people and the blessings he bestows upon them, manifest the perfections of his character and show forth his glory.

entries.title: Psalms 74:19
segments: Thy turtledove; an appellation of endearment, showing God's tender regard for his people.

entries.title: Psalms 74:20
segments:
The covenant; that he made with Abraham and his posterity, especially with reference to the coming of the Messiah. 
 
  The dark places of the earth; those not enlightened by revelation. The psalmist means that the cruelty of these dark places is exercised against God's covenant-people, which is a reason why he should remember his covenant with them. 
 
The covenant which God made with his people, with reference to the Redeemer and the blessings of his universal reign, is ordered in all things and sure; and not one jot or tittle of it will fail till it is all completely accomplished.
